supporting_observations.claim: The recurring proxy connections are to update.datagrid-analytics.com, and endpoint network events attribute corresponding connections to dgupdate.exe running from the installed DataGrid Analytics directory. This matches the approved updater behavior and provides a benign explanation for the periodic-connection alert.

The proxy recorded a successful HTTPS CONNECT tunnel from WS-RIYER-01 to downloads.cloud.com:443. The record does not identify the initiating process or establish what content, if any, was transferred.

Raj Iyer's session launched KB5034441_update.exe from C:\Windows\Temp with medium integrity, with Explorer as its parent; endpoint records show it exited about 65 seconds later. This is not the documented IT patching method, but the records alone do not establish that the executable was malicious.

A Cisco AnyConnect vpnagent.exe process started under SYSTEM on WS-RIYER-01. This conflicts with the supplied environment context that VPN is not used, but the record does not show that a VPN connection was made.
The VPN agent start was recorded shortly after the temporary executable exited. This timing is concerning but does not prove that the executable caused or installed the VPN agent.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show HTTPS CONNECT destinations and tunnel metadata, not encrypted request contents.
The zeek_dns and zeek_ssl queries for WS-RIYER-01 during the review window returned no records.
The available endpoint records do not establish the origin, hash, signature, or contents of KB5034441_update.exe.
The proxy record for downloads.cloud.com does not identify the initiating process, and available records do not link that tunnel to the temporary executable.
The VPN process-start event does not show a VPN connection or resulting remote-access activity.
claims_not_established: That KB5034441_update.exe is malware or was obtained from downloads.cloud.com.
That the Cisco VPN agent connected to a VPN or was installed by the temporary executable.
That data was exfiltrated or that the periodic DataGrid updater traffic was malicious.
That Raj Iyer knowingly initiated the suspicious activity or that the account was compromised.
additional_evidence_needed: Preserve and analyze KB5034441_update.exe, including its hash, signature, origin, and related file-system or browser-download artifacts.
Review software-installation and service-configuration records to determine when and how Cisco AnyConnect was installed or started.
Obtain process-attributed network telemetry and VPN client logs to determine whether the VPN agent connected and to what destination.
Review proxy, browser, and endpoint evidence around the downloads.cloud.com tunnel to identify its initiating process and any transferred content.
